newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso reverses losses to end firm.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso reverses losses to end firm.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed earlier weakness to close firmer on Tuesday after foreign dealers switched from dollars to enter the domestic money market, dealers said.
"Demand for dollars was heavy this morning, but once the peso reached 7.9400 per dollar, they just sold dollars from then on," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 1.6 and 1.5 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8960/7.9000 and 7.8950/7.8980 per dollar.
"The word is two large U.S. players stepped in to sell dollars, either to take part in the (Cetes) auction, or just to dump long positions," another trader said.
Money market traders forecast Banco de Mexico would assign bellether 28-day Cetes rates at an average of 18.19 percent, according to a Reuters survey nN27534540.
This would represent an increase of 12 basis points since last week's auction.
Banco de Mexico was due to announce the results of its weekly government securities auction at 1830 local time/2330 GMT.
Dealers said Wednesday's session could be calmer after uncertainty over the Cetes auction had receded.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 5.7 centavos weaker at 7.9170/7.9220 per dollar after lagging behind the market.
"I don't think the market will be as volatile as it was today. The 48-hour peso could fluctuate between 7.9000/7.9200 per dollar," a dealer said.
